nodes.title: The new feature is well-isolated from the larger codebase
nodes.body: Orientation grounded only in the selected spec assumes the feature is genuinely separable from the absent surrounding codebase. If the feature turns out entangled with code that isn't present, spec-scoped orientation could quietly mislead the user by omitting dependencies living outside the spec. This is the load-bearing bet under TH1.

nodes.title: Selection must stay scoped to the chosen spec
A workspace may hold multiple specs
Orientation targets an isolated new feature inside a larger, absent codebase
nodes.body: The selected spec begins near-empty, but not because the world is greenfield. It describes a relatively well-isolated new feature that lives within a larger existing codebase which is not present in the workspace and not available to read. Orientation therefore cannot lean on inspecting surrounding code; it must work from the selected spec's own graph state. This corrects CTX2's 'new-from-scratch' framing, which conflated 'spec begins near-empty' with 'greenfield'.

nodes.title: Help a user orient inside one workspace

detail.definition: The one spec whose graph and sessions a current interaction targets.

nodes.title: Orientation comes from the selected spec's graph state, not the whole workspace at once

edges.rationale: Re-anchors the context-required-by-goal relation that CTX2 carried.
If the feature is well-isolated, orienting from the selected spec's graph alone is sufficient; isolation is what makes TH1 hold.
